claims.text: The post's title, title tag, meta description and intro frame it as the 10 cloud trends shaping 2027 and beyond (updated edition of the earlier 2026 post).
In 2027, AI agents are moving from writing code to operating infrastructure directly, with humans approving changes rather than authoring every one.
Hyperscaler capital spending, Kubernetes-for-AI adoption, and platform engineering are all accelerating in 2027 alongside the shift to agentic infrastructure.
Last year's edition of this Pulumi post predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade, and the 2026 predictions held up.
Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue (L55 phrasing; L79 says full fiscal-year 2026 Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time).
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion (as of Q2 2026).
AWS's AI business and its custom-silicon (chips) business each passed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner has forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027, and describes cloud as becoming a business necessity by 2028.
According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, cloud value driven by innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings.
According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, high-performing organizations can achieve an EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030 from cloud.
According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, Asia leads in projected cloud value, followed by the US and Europe.

According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, high-ROI organizations excel by aligning cloud strategy with business priorities, building strong cloud foundations, and using modern operating models.
Pulumi Insights + Policies is a unified governance framework that teams use, together with infrastructure as code and automation, to operationalize cloud value.
Hyperscalers are making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history, nearly all centered on AI workloads, inference, and high-performance compute.
AWS reported $42.2 billion in revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest revenue growth since 2021.
AWS's AI business and its chips business (which includes custom Trainium and Graviton silicon) are each growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.

Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026) Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year, up from 40% growth the prior quarter, and Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026, and its backlog was $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had itself already been raised twice in 2026.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.

Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, driven by large-scale AI infrastructure contracts including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals now totaling $75 billion.
Hybrid and multi-cloud strategies are now mainstream.
ResearchAndMarkets projects the hybrid cloud market will grow from $130B to $310–330B by 2030.
According to Mordor Intelligence, 87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.

In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure, with most running more than one cloud (i.e., multi-cloud is the norm among surveyed teams).
Pulumi ran a 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers (the State of Agentic Infrastructure report).
Organizations must deploy workloads across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, on-prem, and edge while maintaining consistent security, compliance and configuration, as AI and regulatory requirements grow.
Pulumi provides infrastructure as code for multi-cloud provisioning, Pulumi Policies for policy-driven guardrails, and internal developer platform capabilities.
According to Gartner, total worldwide AI spending, spanning software, hardware, and services, is forecast to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.

Pulumi's Superintelligence Infrastructure page explains why AI workloads, from pre-training to inference at massive scale, require dynamic infrastructure orchestration rather than static configuration.

Pulumi ESC manages secrets and configuration at scale; Pulumi Insights provides visibility and misconfiguration analysis; Pulumi Policies provide AI-specific guardrails in code, cost detection, and automated compliance protections.
Organizations are increasingly adopting IaC in general-purpose languages to unify development and infrastructure workflows and reduce configuration drift.
Modern IaC integrates with cloud providers and third-party services, including CockroachDB, Confluent Cloud, and Kafka.
Pulumi Insights Discovery improves cloud resource efficiency and visibility.
Pulumi Policy as Code enforces guardrails, cost controls, and regulatory requirements automatically.
Pulumi Policies incorporates AI-driven optimization and insights that help teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates.
Gartner predicts that by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications.
Gartner predicts total spending on securing AI will reach roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Pulumi ESC helps teams centralize and govern credentials, keys, and tokens.

At the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney, Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, said: "[AI]... it doesn't deliver value on its own – AI needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance to enable intelligent, adaptive decisions and actions across the organization."

According to Gartner, by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools for application delivery.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations already have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% are running a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.
The year 2026 (Gartner's target year for 80% of large engineering organizations to have platform engineering teams) has now arrived.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said: "Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects that make software delivery reliable at scale. What's especially notable about this research is how organizations are extending those same platforms to support AI workloads, showing how cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications."

Mid-size to large companies continue to invest in platform engineering practices, with large tech companies as first adopters, providing Internal Developer Platforms to improve developer experience (DX, sometimes called DE or DevEx).

Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 82% agree that AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes, yet manual approval remains close to universal today.
Pulumi's report describes the gap between trust in agents and manual approval practice as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, the share of teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rises from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails in place, keeping the human accountable for what ships.
Pulumi's blog post 'The Agentic Infrastructure Era' argues that AIOps is headed toward a supervised agentic operating model rather than toward faster dashboards and alerting alone.

In 2027, AIOps signals (observability, automation, real-time analytics bridging DevOps, SRE, and IT operations) increasingly feed an agent empowered to act on them, with a person still reviewing the result.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.
The CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.

The CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report says 30% of backend developers now use Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, a decline the report attributes to the technology's growing maturity.

Inference workloads powered by LLMs and GPUs now require low-latency execution closer to the user, pushing organizations to schedule AI pipelines across edge and core clusters, often using Kubernetes as the common control plane for AI cluster orchestration.
Pulumi's blog covers Kubernetes evolving for AI in more depth and has a comparison of Kubernetes IaC tools (best-kubernetes-iac-tools-2026).
Kubernetes will continue its ascent in 2027 and is evolving to support AI through GPU-aware scheduling and more advanced workload orchestration.
Kubernetes will remain a strategic foundation, but operating it effectively now depends on robust automation, strong security controls, and standardized delivery models.

AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams, and the same shift is reaching infrastructure code.

According to Gartner, by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use AI code assistants.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit (announced May 2026).
Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
The July 2026 MCP revision is part of what makes direct action by AI assistants on infrastructure practical.

Pulumi Agent Skills is a recently released collection of infrastructure expertise packaged for use in AI coding assistants, and teaches tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects, reducing hallucination and improving outputs.
Pulumi's Remote MCP Server provides infrastructure access for AI assistants, and Pulumi Neo executes actions with previews, policies, and orchestration.
AI code assistants are no longer experimental and are fast becoming a competitive advantage in cloud software development.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes, and AI now sets the organizing principle for cloud strategy.
Modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
The gap between teams that modernize their cloud operations and those that do not will widen rapidly in 2027 and beyond.
The post's 'updated' frontmatter date is 2026-09-15 while the publish date is 2025-12-04.
